aspects.says: A blocking call inside a parallel stream holds common-pool workers, which the pool does not replace, so other parallel streams and default async tasks wait.
basis: section:A Blocking Call Inside a Parallel Stream Starves Every Other User of the Common Pool

aspects.says: A parallel stream over boxed elements can stay slower than a sequential sum over an int array.
basis: section:Boxed Elements Cost More Than Threads Win Back
aspects.reason: a difference in time only, which a deterministic graded test cannot check; the page shows the measurement

aspects.says: A parallel stream runs on the JVM-wide common ForkJoinPool, availableProcessors() - 1 workers by default, and the thread that calls the terminal operation works as one more.
basis: section:A Parallel Stream Runs on the Common ForkJoinPool, With Its Caller as One More Worker

aspects.says: groupingByConcurrent and toConcurrentMap fill one shared map in the order threads arrive, so groups lose encounter order and a keep-first merge keeps the first to arrive; groupingBy and toMap keep encounter order.
basis: section:groupingByConcurrent Trades the Order Inside Each Group for One Shared Map

aspects.says: A parallel run pays a fixed price before any element is processed, so it pays only when the number of elements times the cost of each outweighs it.
basis: section:Parallel Pays Only When the Work Outweighs Splitting and Merging

aspects.says: The last parallel() or sequential() call sets the mode of the whole pipeline, so a parallel step followed by an ordered one-at-a-time step needs forEachOrdered or two pipelines.
basis: section:One Pipeline Runs in One Mode: the Last parallel() or sequential() Call Wins

aspects.says: findFirst and limit on an ordered parallel stream must respect encounter order, while findAny and limit after unordered() may return any matching elements.
basis: section:Encounter Order Costs Coordination; Give It Up Only Where Nothing Depends On It

aspects.says: A parallel stream started inside a task of your own ForkJoinPool runs in that pool, an undocumented JDK behaviour; another kind of executor does not count, and the pool must be shut down and its failures unwrapped from ExecutionException.
basis: section:Running the Stream Inside Your Own ForkJoinPool Works, but No Document Promises It

aspects.says: ArrayList, arrays and ranges split into halves, while LinkedList and iterate are cut into batches on one thread, which limits the speed-up when the work per element is cheap.
basis: section:The Source Decides How Well the Work Splits
